text: Where does the water you drink actually go?
It soaks up about ninety percent of the water you take in.
Then the large intestine pulls out most of what's left.
Now that water is in your blood, and your blood runs through your kidneys.
Every day, they filter about a hundred and fifty quarts from your blood.
Only one to two quarts become urine.
It flows down two thin tubes, the ureters, into your bladder.
Your bladder holds about one and a half to two cups.
